field.note: Estimated from satellite imagery, not a legal boundary

koppen.name: Humid continental, warm summer
koppen.explain: Cold winters, warm summers, rain all year.

wrbGroup.name: Chernozems
wrbGroup.explain: Dark, humus-rich, usually very fertile soil.

stress.whyShort: Summers are dry enough to stress shallow-rooted crops.
stress.whyFull: In July-August about 175 mm of rain falls but the field loses about 240 mm to evaporation, so soil moisture runs short late in the season. Data: NASA POWER 2001-2020. Confidence: medium.

stress.whyShort: The soil drains well enough and the field is not flat.
stress.whyFull: The wettest month brings about 95 mm of rain, clay content is 30% and the slope is 3.2%, so water rarely stands on the field. Data: NASA POWER 2001-2020, ISRIC SoilGrids. Confidence: medium.

stress.whyShort: Late spring frosts can damage early sowings.
stress.whyFull: Five months have an average minimum temperature at or below 0 °C and April minimum is only 3 °C, so the frost-free period is about 7 months. Data: NASA POWER 2001-2020. Confidence: high.

evidence.label: Months with minimum at or below 0 °C

stress.whyShort: Summers are warm but rarely too hot for crops.
stress.whyFull: The hottest month has an average maximum of 25 °C, below the heat thresholds of the main crops. Data: NASA POWER 2001-2020. Confidence: high.

stress.whyShort: A gentle slope and silty soil let rain wash the top layer away.
stress.whyFull: Slope is 3.2% and silt is 45%, and summer months bring up to 95 mm of rain, which raises water erosion risk on bare soil. Data: elevation API, ISRIC SoilGrids, NASA POWER. Confidence: medium.

stress.whyShort: The soil is rich in humus and close to neutral.
stress.whyFull: Organic carbon is 28 g/kg (range 22-34) and pH is 6.8 (range 6.5-7.1), both inside the comfortable range for most field crops. Data: ISRIC SoilGrids. Confidence: medium.

crops.name: Soybean
crops.why: Fixes nitrogen and breaks the cereal cycle; the 7-month growing season is long enough.

crops.name: Winter wheat
crops.why: Suits pH 6.8 and 681 mm of annual rain; uses winter moisture before the dry July-August.

crops.name: Clover cover crop
crops.why: Covers the soil on the 3.2% slope and adds organic matter.

strategies.title: Keep the current rotation
strategies.summary: Repeat what was grown in the last three years: wheat, then corn with soybean, then fallow.
strategies.why: It already alternates a cereal with a legume, but the fallow year leaves the 3.2% slope bare and one crop covers the whole field in the first year.
benefits: No change in machinery or habits.
The fallow year lets the soil store water.
risks: Bare fallow on a slope loses topsoil in heavy rain.
A single crop on the whole field concentrates weather and disease risk.
dataGaps: Crop shares inside each past year were not entered, so equal shares are assumed.

strategies.title: Balanced rotation
strategies.summary: Three crops every year, with a legume and a cover crop always present.
strategies.why: The 7-month growing season and 681 mm of annual rain suit all three crops, and a legume follows the cereal every year.
benefits: Legumes add nitrogen for the following cereal.
Changing crop families every year interrupts pest and disease cycles.
Clover keeps part of the field covered.
risks: Check that there is a local market for soybean and pea.
Three crops a year need more planning of sowing and harvest dates.
dataGaps: Climate is a 2001-2020 average on a coarse grid of about 50 km.

strategies.title: Soil-first rotation
strategies.summary: More cover crop and legumes to protect the slope and build organic matter.
strategies.why: Slope 3.2% and silt 45% give a moderate erosion risk (score 45); keeping about a third of the field under clover reduces the time soil is bare.
benefits: Least bare soil of the three strategies.
Builds organic matter and improves water infiltration.
risks: A smaller share of cash crops; clover needs a use as forage or green manure.
Cover crops use some soil water before the dry July-August.
dataGaps: Soil values are model estimates at about 250 m, not a lab analysis of this field.

avoid.name: Corn (maize)
avoid.why: Corn (maize) was grown here last year: repeating it builds up its diseases, pests and weeds.

avoid.name: Rice
avoid.why: Rice: rainfall of 681 mm per year is too low (it needs 1000-4000 mm, best 1500-2000 mm).

tillage.title: Reduce ploughing
tillage.simple: Disturb the soil less so rain does not wash it away.
tillage.expert: Shift to strip-till or no-till; slope 3.2% and silt 45% raise erosion risk.
tillage.why: Slope 3.2% and silt 45% make bare soil easy to wash away.

tillage.title: Leave crop residue on the field
tillage.simple: Leave straw and stalks on the surface to keep the soil moist.
tillage.expert: Keep at least 30% residue cover after harvest to cut evaporation during July-August.
tillage.why: In July-August rain is about 175 mm against about 240 mm of evaporation.

tillage.title: Sow cover crops
tillage.simple: Do not leave the field bare between main crops.
tillage.expert: Sow clover or a cover-crop mix after early-harvested cereals to protect the 3.2% slope.
tillage.why: Erosion risk is moderate (score 45) and bare soil is the main driver.

warnings: Check local disease pressure with an agronomist.
assumptions: Climate is the 2001-2020 average, not a forecast.
Soil values are model estimates at about 250 m resolution, not a lab analysis of this field.

disclaimer: This tool supports decisions and does not replace a local agronomist.
